summary: Three times a year, money was taken out of the shekalim room to buy korbanos. Rabbi Akiva says these are also the times for maaser of animals, and other Rabbis give different dates.

chunks.he: בִּשְׁלשָׁה פְּרָקִים בַּשָּׁנָה, תּוֹרְמִין אֶת הַלִּשְׁכָּה,
chunks.en: Three times a year they take money out of the lishkah:
chunks.st: On three occasions during the year the ceremony of the collection of the Temple treasury chamber is performed. During the ceremony,
chunks.stMore: a priest enters the treasury chamber with three containers, lifts up [torem] some of the coins, and places them in the containers. These funds, known as the collection of the chamber, are used to purchase animals for communal offerings and other needs of the Temple.

words.note: The room in the Beis HaMikdash where the shekalim were kept.

chunks.en: half a month before Pesach,
chunks.st: These three occasions are: Half a month, fifteen days, before Passover, on the day before the first of the month of Nisan;

chunks.en: half a month before Shavuos,
chunks.st: half a month before Shavuot, on or around the twentieth of Iyar;

chunks.en: and half a month before Sukkos.
chunks.st: half a month before the festival of Sukkot, on the day before Rosh HaShana.

chunks.en: These are also the set times for maaser of animals.
chunks.st: These three days are also the due dates that were established by the Sages for the setting aside of animal tithes.
chunks.stMore: On each of these days one is obligated to tithe the animals that were born during the intervening period, and it is prohibited for him to eat or sell them until he does so.

words.note: Giving every tenth new animal as a korban.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Akiva says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

chunks.en: Ben Azzai says,
chunks.st: Ben Azzai says
chunks.stMore: that the dates established by the Sages for the setting aside of animal tithes are

chunks.en: on the twenty-ninth of Adar,
chunks.st: the twenty-ninth of Adar,

chunks.en: on the first of Sivan, and on the twenty-ninth of Av.
chunks.st: the first of Sivan, and the twenty-ninth of Av.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say that the dates for the animal tithes are

chunks.en: on the first of Nisan, on the first of Sivan,
chunks.st: the first of Nisan, the first of Sivan,

chunks.en: and on the twenty-ninth of Elul.
chunks.st: and the twenty-ninth of Elul.

chunks.he: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְתִשְׁעָה בֶּאֱלוּל,
chunks.en: Why did they say the twenty-ninth of Elul
chunks.st: And why did Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say the twenty-ninth of Elul

chunks.en: and not the first of Tishrei?
chunks.st: and not the first of Tishrei, as they said the first of Nisan and Sivan?

chunks.en: Because it is Yom Tov,
chunks.explain: The first of Tishrei is Rosh Hashanah.
chunks.st: Because the first of Tishrei is the festival of Rosh HaShana,

chunks.en: and we may not give maaser on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: and it is not permitted to tithe on a Festival.

chunks.en: So they made it earlier, on the twenty-ninth of Elul.
chunks.st: Therefore, the Sages advanced the day of tithing the animals born over the course of the summer to the twenty-ninth of Elul.

summary: The money was taken out with three baskets marked with letters. The one taking it wore clothes with no place to hide coins, so no one would suspect him of stealing.

chunks.en: With three baskets
chunks.st: The funds are collected from the Temple treasury chamber with three baskets,

chunks.en: each holding three se'ah, they take money out of the lishkah.
chunks.st: each measuring three se’a.

words.note: A measure for how much a basket holds.

chunks.en: And on them is written Alef, Beis, Gimmel.
chunks.st: On the baskets is written, respectively, alef, beit, gimmel,
chunks.stMore: based on the order in which the baskets are filled, to indicate from which basket coins should be taken to buy sacrifices. The coins were used in the order of their collection.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael says:

chunks.he: יְוָנִית כָּתוּב בָּהֶן אָלפ"א בֵית"א גָמל"א.
chunks.en: In Greek is written on them Alfa, Beta, Gamma.
chunks.st: The letters written on them were in Greek, alfa, beta, gamma.

chunks.he: אֵין הַתּוֹרֵם נִכְנָס לֹא בְּפַרְגּוֹד חָפוּת,
chunks.en: The one taking out the money may not go in wearing a garment with folds,
chunks.explain: Folds where coins could be hidden.
chunks.st: The one who collects the funds from the chamber must not enter while wearing a cuffed garment [ḥafut],

chunks.en: and not with a shoe, and not with a sandal,
chunks.st: and not with a shoe, and not with a sandal,

chunks.en: and not with tefillin, and not with a kamei'a.
chunks.explain: All these have places where a coin could be hidden.
chunks.st: and not with phylacteries, and not with an amulet,
chunks.stMore: since all of these have places into which money can be inserted.

words.note: A small charm people wore for protection.

chunks.en: Maybe he will become poor,
chunks.st: The concern is that perhaps the one collecting the funds will one day become poor,

chunks.en: and people will say he became poor because of a sin with the lishkah money.
chunks.st: and people will say that it is because of the sin of stealing the shekels of the chamber that he became poor,
chunks.stMore: as they will suspect that he stole money and hid it in those places.

chunks.en: Or maybe he will become rich,
chunks.st: Or perhaps he will become rich

chunks.en: and people will say he became rich from the lishkah money.
chunks.st: and people will say that he became rich from stealing the funds of the chamber, even though he did not actually do so.
chunks.stMore: Even though one should not suspect someone of stealing consecrated shekels, the one collecting the funds from the chamber must nevertheless take these precautions,

chunks.he: לְפִי שֶׁאָדָם צָרִיךְ לָצֵאת יְדֵי הַבְּרִיּוֹת
chunks.en: Because a person must make sure people see he is innocent,
chunks.st: as a person must appear justified before people

chunks.en: just as he must be innocent before Hashem,
chunks.st: just as he must appear justified before the Omnipresent [HaMakom],

chunks.he: שְׁנֶּאֱמַר (במדבר לב) וִהְיִיתֶם נְקִיִים מֵיְיָ וּמִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
chunks.en: as the pasuk says, "You shall be clean before Hashem and before Yisrael."
chunks.st: and it is stated: “And you shall be guiltless before the Lord and before Israel”
chunks.stMore: (Numbers 32:22). From here it may be inferred that it is not enough to be innocent before God; one must also be innocent before the Jewish people. Even in situations where there is little concern that one may commit a sin, the proper course is to remain above any possible suspicion of misconduct.

chunks.en: And it says, "And find favor
chunks.st: And the verse states: “So shall you find grace

chunks.en: and good sense in the eyes of G-d and people."
chunks.st: and good understanding in the sight of God and man” (Proverbs 3:4).

summary: Members of Rabban Gamliel's family wanted their own half-shekel to be used for the korbanos, so they tossed it right in front of the one taking out the money. Before he took the money, he asked permission three times.
stIntro: In order to indicate the importance that was attached to the ceremony of the collection of the Temple treasury chamber, the mishna relates that the members

chunks.en: Someone from the family of Rabban Gamliel
chunks.st: of the house of Rabban Gamliel
chunks.stMore: desired that their shekels be the ones collected from the chamber and used for the purchase of the communal offerings.

chunks.en: would come in with his half-shekel between his fingers,
chunks.st: Each of them would therefore come to the Temple specifically on the day of the ceremony of the collection of the chamber, enter the chamber with his shekel between his fingers,

chunks.en: and throw it in front of the one taking out the money.
chunks.st: and toss it in front of the one collecting
chunks.stMore: the money so that he would see it and place it in the basket containing the money to be taken out of the chamber.

chunks.en: And the one taking out the money would mean to push it into the basket.
chunks.st: Understanding what was happening, the one collecting the money from the chamber would purposely push this shekel into the basket, so that it would later be used to buy communal offerings.

chunks.he: אֵין הַתּוֹרֵם תּוֹרֵם עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר לָהֶם,
chunks.en: The one taking out the money does not take it until he says to them,
chunks.st: The one collecting the funds from the chamber may not begin to collect the money until he asks the Temple treasurers three times:

chunks.en: "Shall I take?" And they say to him,
chunks.st: Shall I collect the funds, and they say to him:

chunks.en: "Take, take, take," three times.
chunks.st: Collect them, collect them, collect them, three times.

summary: After taking money from each big basket, the one taking it covered the basket so he would not take from it again. Each basket was taken for the sake of Jews in a different place.
stIntro: The coins were stored in the Temple treasury in three large baskets, each measuring nine se’a. In the collection of the chamber ceremony, coins were removed from these baskets and placed in smaller baskets of three se’a each that were marked with letters (see the previous mishna on daf 8a).

chunks.en: He took money from the first basket and covered it with leather covers.
chunks.st: After he collected the funds from the first large basket and put them into one of the smaller baskets labeled with the letter alef, he immediately covered with a leather cover the large basket from which he had removed the money.

chunks.en: From the second, and covered it with leather covers.
chunks.st: After collecting funds from the second large basket, he covered it with a leather cover as well.

chunks.en: The third he did not cover.
chunks.st: But after collecting funds from the third large basket, he did not cover it.

chunks.he: שֶׁמָּא יִשְׁכַּח וְיִתְרֹם מִן הַדָּבָר הַתָּרוּם.
chunks.en: He covered them in case he forgets and takes again from a basket he already took from.
chunks.st: The mishna asks: Why did he cover the first two baskets? In order to mark them as already having had funds collected from them. In this way, there was no concern that perhaps he would forget and once again collect funds from a basket from which funds had already been collected.

chunks.he: תָּרַם אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה לְשֵׁם אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
chunks.en: He took from the first one for the sake of Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.st: The mishna specifies the intent of the one collecting the funds from the baskets as he does so: He collected funds from the first basket on behalf of the people living in Eretz Yisrael;

chunks.en: the second one for the walled cities near it,
chunks.st: from the second basket on behalf of the people living in the cities near Eretz Yisrael;

chunks.en: and the third one for the sake of Bavel,
chunks.st: and from the third basket on behalf of the people living in Babylonia,

chunks.en: and for the sake of Madai,
chunks.st: and on behalf of the people living in Media,

chunks.en: and for the sake of faraway countries.
chunks.st: and on behalf of the people living in the distant countries.
